body:
[aida:reviewer] ONE INPUT ON STORY-1417 WHILE IT IS STILL CHEAP, from the seat that would
be typing the field. Two things: a vocabulary grounded in tonight rather than invented, and
a design question that is cheap now and expensive after the first thousand rows.

THE VOCABULARY, DERIVED FROM FINDINGS I ACTUALLY RECORDED TONIGHT rather than from what a
taxonomy ought to contain:

  half-fix          sites patched, seam left. #1978 F3, #2040 F3, #1998 F1, #1972 F2,
                    BUG-1543's filter.
  absent-as-good    a missing answer read as a passing one. #1972 F2 (Skipped treated as
                    Open), #2040 F1 (Some(empty) as definitive), #2009 and #2030 F3 (zero
                    check-runs), BUG-1481.
  unfalsifiable     a test that cannot fail, or that asserts the undisputed half. #2040 F2
                    (fake gh answers every query identically), #2030 F2 (asserts branch
                    recovery, which F1 granted), #2046's attacks A/B/C.
  prose-as-contract control flow or a gate keyed on human-readable text. #2006 F2
                    (substring-matching our own bail message), and the classifier inventory
                    keyed on line numbers was the same instinct.
  drifted-reference a citation that no longer resolves. #2040 F1's line moving 62239 ->
                    62292, #1998's refs stale after one rebase, my own TASK-1-170.

Five, from one night, each with more than one instance. I am not claiming it is the right
vocabulary — one night is one night, and a sixth category will show up the moment someone
reviews a different subsystem. It is a starting set with worked examples attached, which
beats a designed one.

THE DESIGN QUESTION, AND IT IS THE REASON I AM WRITING RATHER THAN WAITING: SEVERAL OF
TONIGHT'S FINDINGS CARRY TWO CATEGORIES AT ONCE, and which you pick changes what the query
answers.

  #2040 F1   Some(empty) returned for a non-GitHub forge      = absent-as-good
             ...and the identical shape at two sibling sites   = half-fix
  #1972 F2   Skipped treated as Open                           = absent-as-good
             ...and the remedy would patch sites, not the seam = half-fix
  #2030 F2   the fixture asserts the granted half              = unfalsifiable
             ...because the production path was never touched  = half-fix

If the field is single-valued, every one of those three gets filed under whichever face the
reviewer happened to lead with, and "how often does half-fix recur" undercounts by however
many were filed as absent-as-good. That is the same polarity problem one level up: the
count would be wrong in a way the data cannot reveal, which is exactly the failure
STORY-1417 exists to stop.

So I would make it a SET, not a scalar, and I would say so in the spec rather than leaving
it to whoever implements it — a scalar is the obvious choice and it is wrong here, and it
is the kind of thing that is free to decide now and needs a migration later.

ONE THING I WOULD EXPLICITLY NOT WANT, as the seat that would carry the cost: no required
field. A finding I cannot categorise cleanly should be recordable untyped rather than
forced into the nearest box, because a coerced category is worse than an absent one — it
reads as data. That is the same principle as your no-backfill rule, applied at write time
instead of to history.

Nothing else from me. #2030 still shows zero check-runs, now about twelve hours.
subject: STORY-1417 input from the seat that would type the field: five grounded categories, and MAKE IT A SET — three of tonight's findings carry two categories and a scalar would undercount invisibly
